generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the work you are already doing. Almost every assignment you take on rests on sources: an essay built on evidence, a report that cites studies, a project that needs background reading all begin with a search. The students who treat finding sources as a skill, and run it on purpose, are the ones whose work rests on better evidence rather than whatever came up first. Treat what follows as being about your own essays, reports and reading, not about study in the abstract.

The same habit runs through professional practice. Wherever you need to answer a question, make a case, or decide something, you first have to find and weigh good evidence. The ability to search well, choose the right terms and judge what you find is one you keep long after you graduate.
